commit.subject: Cleanup lint issues with uses of testify in Go code
commit.message:
Cleanup lint issues with uses of testify in Go code

Ran testifylint (https://github.com/Antonboom/testifylint) over our
tests to see what issues it would detect, since testify has some
inconsistent APIs, e.g. .Equal(expect, real), but .Len(obj, count), so
it is easy to get args reversed or miss a better function to use.

It found mostly minor things, like being able use .Len() instead of
.Equal(..., len(foo)) or using .NoError() instead of .Nil() on errors,
and a bunch of .Equal() calls that should be reversed.

It did get a number of things wrong that I had to revert, and missed a
number potential cleanups (like specific cases it could be using
.NoError() or .Len() even though it identified other cases in the same
file), so I don't think I would recommend us adding it to our
presubmit or CI.

It is a useful tool for checking your code style, but I don't think it
is good enough at this point to be blocking CLs or be run in an
automated fashion.

Change-Id: Ib44412442af82cf3ab3bf04de7c4d68fabb1f2ca

commit.subject: [tint][val] Fix validation of fixed operand count instructions
commit.message:
[tint][val] Fix validation of fixed operand count instructions

CheckBinary and CheckUnary are currently using the wrong helpers, and
thus do not validate the number of operands are exactly what is
expected. Additional operands are let through, and don't have their
type checked at all, which can lead to crashes later on.

This patch changes them to check for exactly the correct number of
operands. It also adds related test cases to coverage various
malformed inputs that were missing (and check valid inputs are
accepted).

Fixes: 436474475
Change-Id: Iecf9e2dae55565f99b88aa6f6b18aa72f99d84f3

commit.subject: [dawn][vk] Enable bindless using "descriptor indexing"
commit.message:
[dawn][vk] Enable bindless using "descriptor indexing"

Vulkan's equivalent of bindless is called "descriptor indexing" and a
soup of features and limits. Add support for this Vulkan feature and
gate WebGPU's bindless on a bunch of features and limits.

Note that "robustBufferAccessUpdateAfterBind" is a device property that
has implication for robustness when bindless is available. It will be
handled in a future CL and is not handled here.

Bug: 435251399
Change-Id: I9e77026c53b83dc72b30532c12541bd6193871d1

commit.subject: Disable spurious thread-safety analysis warnings
commit.message:
Disable spurious thread-safety analysis warnings

The WaitListEvent::WaitAny method conditionally locks event mutexes.
Clangs static analysis doesn't understand the pattern, and generates
spurious warnings, which trigger errors.

Bug: 435680470
Change-Id: Ia8c00656829cc2b650073ea1ac671583e9342179

commit.subject: [tint] Polyfill Unpack2x16Snorm for mac AMD
commit.message:
[tint] Polyfill Unpack2x16Snorm for mac AMD

Unpack2x16Snorm appears to simply be inaccurate by >= 7ulp whereas in
wgsl we specify 3 ulp.

We can either polyfill (aka this CL) or change the wgsl spec to
accept this new range (probably undesired).

Bug: 407109055

commit.subject: Kotlin: fix intermittent crashing in webGPU.close()
commit.message:
Kotlin: fix intermittent crashing in webGPU.close()

I fixed a bug where the isClosing flag wasn't set (this can stop
crashing in the event polling loop).

Currently if device.close() (which calls wgpuDeviceRelease) is called
this is kills the thread. I don't know why.

On the other hand, if I don't call wgpuDeviceRelease I am able to bring
down the surface, the instance and the adapter, which is an
improvement.

https: //dawn-android-samples.googlesource.com/dawn-demo/+/refs/heads/main

commit.subject: Fix ubsan problems for Tier2 RW storage texture tests
commit.message:
Fix ubsan problems for Tier2 RW storage texture tests

Previously, the test code tried to write uint32_t and other
32-bit scalars on unaligned addresses. This occured when computing
expected values.

Instead, refactor the expected-value function to take an optional
value offset, so the function can be used to generate the initial
buffer and the expected values.

Fixed: crbug.com/438176030
Change-Id: I6a6a6964998ddfecd419a3f22b577d0913b9b736

commit.subject: Patch 2/8: Implement core read/write functions for FSTestOSWrapper
commit.message:
Patch 2/8: Implement core read/write functions for FSTestOSWrapper

Implements ReadFile and WriteFile and adds testing for them, since
they are needed to test each other, and pretty much all of the other
functions.

Also implements MkdirAll, since it is needed in one of the testing
helpers, but does not include tests for it, since its tests require
other functions to be implemented. There is effectively a cycle in the
dependency graph between functions and their tests here that needs to
be broken to avoid a large monolithic patch.

Bug: 436025865
Change-Id: I109dd0a071b23a514120052549c800a007c64ee8

[dawn][native] Factor the defaulting in FillLimits

require the same kind of defaulting as
DawnTexelCopyBufferRowAlignmentsLimits and DawnHostMappedPointerLimits.
Add a polymorphic helper function that does this so that no more
copy-pasting is needed.

commit.subject: Patch 1/8: Implement FSTestOSWrapper foundations
commit.message:
Patch 1/8: Implement FSTestOSWrapper foundations

Defines a testing/fstest based implementation of the OSWrapper
interface, FSTestOSWrapper. This is a stub implementation with minimal
amount of the constructor and utility functions needed, otherwise
methods panic with a message about not being implemented.

Implemented all of the various testing helpers that will be needed in
future CLs in fstestoswrapper_test.go

Renamed the test names in memmaposwrapper_test.go to be prefixed with
the specific implementation being tested, so that testing logs are
easier to read.

Bug: 436025865
Change-Id: I17dda6488b9d5c88049f09087105cf2ed34cc07d

commit.message:
Patch 1/8: Implement FSTestOSWrapper foundations

Defines a testing/fstest based implementation of the OSWrapper
interface, FSTestOSWrapper. This is a stub implementation with minimal
amount of the constructor and utility functions needed, otherwise
methods panic with a message about not being implemented.

Implemented all of the various testing helpers that will be needed in
future CLs in fstestoswrapper_test.go

Renamed the test names in memmaposwrapper_test.go to be prefixed with
the specific implementation being tested, so that testing logs are
easier to read.

Bug: 436025865
Change-Id: I17dda6488b9d5c88049f09087105cf2ed34cc07d

commit.subject: Implement hashing and equality for Tint MSL Options and its member types
commit.message:
Implement hashing and equality for Tint MSL Options and its member types

Add TINT_REFLECT_EQUALS and TINT_REFLECT_HASH_CODE helper macros that
generate operator== and HashCode implementations based on reflected
fields. Also, add missing Hash specializations for unordered_map/set and
optional.

Will be used for caching MTLLibrary objects based on a MetalShaderParams
key type that includes the Tint MSL Options.

Bug: 42241511
Change-Id: I6a6a6964d2f6d2d705066524824dd643c865f480

commit.subject: [spirv-reader] Build swizzles for consecutive shuffle accesses
commit.message:
[spirv-reader] Build swizzles for consecutive shuffle accesses

For an OpVectorShuffle that accesses both vectors, this allows us to
produce swizzles for consecutive indices that fall within the same
vector, which can significantly reduce the size of the generated WGSL
for some shaders.

Fixed: 437398335
Change-Id: I09a6b9eb60ad7314e32150869a8910e9b5fbb430

commit.message:
[dawn] Switch SPIR-V ingestion to Tint IR flow

Remove a validation test that was requiring is to produce a graceful
error for arrayed multisampled textures. We do fail for that case, but
with an ICE that crashes the process. This seems fine for now, and
this commit slightly improves that message by crashing earlier.

Fixed: 436823060
Change-Id: Icfd760bd9b6ac7632fc33c163665f420e6b35745

commit.subject: [dawn] Switch SPIR-V ingestion to Tint IR flow
commit.message:
[dawn] Switch SPIR-V ingestion to Tint IR flow

Add a validation step after we have lowered to core IR to fail
gracefully on things that would otherwise cause ICEs when converting
to WGSL.

Reject arrayed multisampled images in the IR validator as they are not
supported in WGSL or needed by any of our flows.

Fixed: 436823060
Change-Id: Icfd760bd9b6ac7632fc33c163665f420e6b35745

dawn/wire: Move all the members of `WriteHandle` to private

the land of the related changes in Chromium. Because `mTargetData`
and `mDataLength` may not be set together, we cannot put them into
one `std::span`.

commit.subject: Reapply "Use SearchPaths to load DX compiler DLLs"
commit.message:
Reapply "Use SearchPaths to load DX compiler DLLs"

This reverts commit 80062b708e44aa4d8c48e555ed0cc801396069f6.

It was reverted because EGL tests were failing on the Dawn -> Chromium
roll.  Those should now be fixed via "Fix EGLImage test failures"
https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/256518

Reapply https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/251714
>     Use SearchPaths to load DX compiler DLLs
>
>     Previously, DX compiler DLLs were loaded using LoadLibrary with no path.
>     For better security, load DX compiler DLLs using full paths, with
>     SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR | SEARCH_DEFAULT_DIRS.
>
>     Add dawn_force_system_component_load for projects (like Skia) which
>     require that Dawn load all compiler DLL from System32. Best security
>     is to leave the default value which (now) loads employs the search
>     path.
>
>     Bug:356665092
>     Change-Id: Ib04a2aba3697bbfa1a4d16b9320e3f09e4718798
>     Reviewed-on: https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/251714
>     Commit-Queue: Rafael Cintron <rafael.cintron@microsoft.com>
>     Reviewed-by: Corentin Wallez <cwallez@chromium.org>
>     Reviewed-by: Loko Kung <lokokung@google.com>

Change-Id: I7190f23f8843bf6b610f9e71affe8e6e52290f62

commit.subject: [tint] Always expose SpirvToWgsl
commit.message:
[tint] Always expose SpirvToWgsl

An external user that includes `tint.h` will not have defined the
macros needed to enable this function. We should not require that
external users always build their code with the same macros that Tint
was built with.

Instead, this change always exposes SpirvToWgsl, which will then
return an error if Tint itself was not built with the required macros.

Change-Id: I154a3f91aa5bedb690b2d98139c44cf4c569e796

commit.subject: [dawn][d3d12] Fix texture component swizzle for stencil formats
commit.message:
[dawn][d3d12] Fix texture component swizzle for stencil formats

The existing logic for composing the texture component swizzle for
stencil formats was incorrect. It did not properly apply the existing
texture view's swizzle. This patch refactors the code to use a new
helper function, `ComposeSwizzle`, that correctly combines the base
texture swizzle with the view's swizzle. This ensures that the texture
components are correctly remapped when a texture view is created for a
stencil format.

Bug: 414312052
Change-Id: I8ffe83cad83e108bb7074138e62c3215f41ef67e

commit.message:
[dawn][d3d12] Fix texture component swizzle for stencil formats

The existing logic for composing the texture component swizzle for
stencil formats was incorrect. It did not properly apply the existing
texture view's swizzle. This patch refactors the code to use a new
helper function, `ComposeSwizzle`, that correctly combines the base
texture swizzle with the view's swizzle. This ensures that the texture
components are correctly remapped when a texture view is created for a
stencil format.

Bug: 414312052

commit.subject: Use SearchPaths to load DX compiler DLLs
commit.message:
Use SearchPaths to load DX compiler DLLs

Previously, DX compiler DLLs were loaded using LoadLibrary with no path.
For better security, load DX compiler DLLs using full paths, with
SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR | SEARCH_DEFAULT_DIRS.

Add dawn_force_system_component_load for projects (like Skia) which
require that Dawn load all compiler DLL from System32. Best security
is to leave the default value which (now) loads employs the search
path.

Bug:356665092
Change-Id: Ib04a2aba3697bbfa1a4d16b9320e3f09e4718798

commit.subject: [spirv-reader] Do not change access mode used for type map for handles
commit.message:
[spirv-reader] Do not change access mode used for type map for handles

The access mode that we use to key into the type map needs to use the
actual access mode that we are going to use for the image type,
otherwise we will have a collision when the same SPIR-V type is used
in two different variables with two different access mode.

We already handle setting the access mode for image types when we
actually emit the type, so we don't need to change anything for the
type map key.

Fixed: 437093642
Change-Id: I90b6e383c6ad0bc563fcea43ee698f7a81723254

commit.subject: Reland "Convert Standalone Builders to chromium wrappers"
commit.message:
Reland "Convert Standalone Builders to chromium wrappers"

This is a reland of commit 2be761ae0434470139671d5ee0d87d7ee95b27b9

Original change's description:
> Convert Standalone Builders to chromium wrappers
>
> Converts the experimental standalone Dawn builders to use the wrappers
> provided by the @chromium-luci package. This allows us to fully define
> builders src-side instead of having to split them between the Dawn repo
> and the build repo.
>
> Tests are still defined using the older buildbot JSON approach since
> we want to keep the Swarming dimensions in sync with Chromium's. We may
> be able to roll in Starlark-defined dimensions at some point in the
> future, but the JSON approach should work until that is demonstrated
> to work.
>
> Should be landed in conjunction with crrev.com/c/6808555 to fully move
> the standalone Dawn builders into the Dawn repo.
>
> Bug: 385317083

commit.subject: Stop requiring Device for AttachmentState creation
commit.message:
Stop requiring Device for AttachmentState creation

AttachmentStates inherited from ObjectBase, which requires them to hold
a Ref to a Device, but they never actually used it outside of one
feature check in a debug message. This change switches them to inherit
from RefCounted, which avoids the need to track the Device. This in turn
speeds up the creation of the AttachmentStates Blueprints used to query
the cached AttachmentStates.

Bug: 436878521
Change-Id: Iefff5d4e12141b7072fd244221ba113456412ac0

commit.subject: [spirv-reader][ir] Fix constant-id check for NonUniform calls.
commit.message:
[spirv-reader][ir] Fix constant-id check for NonUniform calls.

The original check that the `value` was constant was a) too broadly
applied and b) the wrong operand to check. This Cl constrains the check
to just the Broadcast, QuadBroadcast and QuadSwap instructions and
corrects the check to use the `Invocation Id` instead of the `Value`.

Fixed: 432807736
Change-Id: I643d3e44a77aa65ed8f9ce26c1fb9ade2c5b8fd6

commit.subject: [spirv-reader][ir] Fix issue with SampledImage registration.
commit.message:
[spirv-reader][ir] Fix issue with SampledImage registration.

When converting user calls, we may fork functions which take image
parameters. This means, if the function has a `SampledImage` we won't
have registered it in the `SampledImage` hash. To fix this, when
re-iterating over the instructions, re-record any `SampledImage`
instructions.

Fixed: 430358345
Change-Id: I2dbdda8cbb7276ab7a8f129ebe1ef40cf6c7a2d0

commit.message:
[emscripten] Explain distributions better in the readme

Explain the three methods of distribution and explicitly list the steps
needed for each one. This makes the Emdawnwebgpu readme make more sense
regardless of what context it's read in:

- inside the remoteport file vendored in Emscripten
- inside the remoteport file in our GitHub release
- in the README.md in the zip in our GitHub release
- in the link from our GitHub release notes
- in the Dawn source

Fixed: 415224043
Change-Id: I560ec0293961e925426c6662c0b05fcf80711da3

commit.subject: Convert Standalone Builders to chromium wrappers
commit.message:
Convert Standalone Builders to chromium wrappers

Converts the experimental standalone Dawn builders to use the wrappers
provided by the @chromium-luci package. This allows us to fully define
builders src-side instead of having to split them between the Dawn repo
and the build repo.

Tests are still defined using the older buildbot JSON approach since
we want to keep the Swarming dimensions in sync with Chromium's. We may
be able to roll in Starlark-defined dimensions at some point in the
future, but the JSON approach should work until that is demonstrated
to work.

Should be landed in conjunction with crrev.com/c/6808555 to fully move
the standalone Dawn builders into the Dawn repo.

Bug: 385317083
Change-Id: I818299ffc1e66a8f9ab946fb1177fe039a654565

commit.subject: [wgsl] Do not automatically enable f16 for subgroups
commit.message:
[wgsl] Do not automatically enable f16 for subgroups

Subgroup builtins do not need the f16 extension. If the f16 overloads
are used, the f16 extension would have been enabled when we emitted
the f16 type or an f16 constant.

commit.subject: [emscripten] Fix enum tables to avoid 328k commas
commit.message:
[emscripten] Fix enum tables to avoid 328k commas

The string-to-int tables get evaluated and re-serialized during the
Emscripten build, resulting in the Object.assign-based sparse array
for FeatureName getting turned into a [a,,,,,,,,,,,,,b] sparse array
literal.

Fix by using reverse string-to-int tables instead of indexOf.

Fixed: 435879324
Bug: 436751438, b/436846761
Change-Id: Ic8a6b61266d3b8271f9f92d44d4af2e0e79e9818

commit.subject: Rolling build dependencies
commit.message:
Rolling build dependencies

Rolls a bunch of build dependencies, which also required:

 - Rolling ANGLE and VMA for a suppression of -Wthread-safety-analysis
 - Rolling googletest for a narrowing warning fix.
 - Updating the Abseil BUILD.gn files.
 - Adding the download of objdump as the toolchain now uses llvm-otool.
 - Disabling the use of libatomic that we don't have as a dep.
 - Disable -Wnrvo that warns when RVO cannot be applied and has a ton of
   false positives (cases we don't care to fix).
 - Suppress an MSVC warning for Abseil's symbolize_win32.cc that includes
   conflicting Windows headers.
 - Silence warnings about MTLCompileOptions.fastMathEnabled being
   deprecated since we cannot remove it until after we require macOS
   15.0.
 - mac_min_sdk defaults to 12 (overriding Chrome's 15)
 - Mac bot candidates: remove Mac-11, add Mac-15

commit.subject: Rolling build dependencies
commit.message:
Rolling build dependencies

Rolls a bunch of build dependencies, which also required:

 - Rolling ANGLE and VMA for a suppression of -Wthread-safety-analysis
 - Rolling googletest for a narrowing warning fix.
 - Updating the Abseil BUILD.gn files.
 - Adding the download of objdump as the toolchain now uses llvm-otool.
 - Disabling the use of libatomic that we don't have as a dep.
 - Disable -Wnrvo that warns when RVO cannot be applied and has a ton of
   false positives (cases we don't care to fix).
 - Suppress an MSVC warning for Abseil's symbolize_win32.cc that includes
   conflicting Windows headers.
 - Silence warnings about MTLCompileOptions.fastMathEnabled being
   deprecated since we cannot remove it until after we require macOS
   15.0.
 - mac_min_sdk defaults to 12 (overriding Chrome's 15)
 - Mac bot candidates: remove Mac-11, add Mac-15

commit.subject: Rolling build dependencies
commit.message:
Rolling build dependencies

Rolls a bunch of build dependencies, which also required:

 - Rolling ANGLE and VMA for a suppression of -Wthread-safety-analysis
 - Rolling googletest for a narrowing warning fix.
 - Updating the Abseil BUILD.gn files.
 - Adding the download of objdump as the toolchain now uses llvm-otool.
 - Disabling the use of libatomic that we don't have as a dep.
 - Disable -Wnrvo that warns when RVO cannot be applied and has a ton of
   false positives (cases we don't care to fix).
 - Suppress an MSVC warning for Abseil's symbolize_win32.cc that includes
   conflicting Windows headers.
 - Silence warnings about MTLCompileOptions.fastMathEnabled being
   deprecated since we cannot remove it until after we require macOS
   15.0.
 - mac_min_sdk defaults to 12 (overriding Chrome's 15)
 - Mac bot candidates: remove Mac-11, add Mac-15

commit.subject: Rolling build dependencies
commit.message:
Rolling build dependencies

Rolls a bunch of build dependencies, which also required:

 - Rolling ANGLE and VMA for a suppression of -Wthread-safety-analysis
 - Rolling googletest for a narrowing warning fix.
 - Updating the Abseil BUILD.gn files.
 - Adding the download of objdump as the toolchain now uses llvm-otool.
 - Disabling the use of libatomic that we don't have as a dep.
 - Disable -Wnrvo that warns when RVO cannot be applied and has a ton of
   false positives (cases we don't care to fix).
 - Suppress an MSVC warning for Abseil's symbolize_win32.cc that includes
   conflicting Windows headers.
 - Silence warnings about MTLCompileOptions.fastMathEnabled being
   deprecated since we cannot remove it until after we require macOS
   15.0.
 - mac_min_sdk defaults to 12 (overriding Chrome's 15)
 - Mac bot candidates: remove Mac-11, add Mac-15

commit.subject: Rolling build dependencies
commit.message:
Rolling build dependencies

Rolls a bunch of build dependencies, which also required:

 - Rolling ANGLE and VMA for a suppression of -Wthread-safety-analysis
 - Rolling googletest for a narrowing warning fix.
 - Updating the Abseil BUILD.gn files.
 - Adding the download of objdump as the toolchain now uses llvm-otool.
 - Disabling the use of libatomic that we don't have as a dep.
 - Disable -Wnrvo that warns when RVO cannot be applied and has a ton of
   false positives (cases we don't care to fix).
 - Suppress an MSVC warning for Abseil's symbolize_win32.cc that includes
   conflicting Windows headers.
 - Silence warnings about MTLCompileOptions.fastMathEnabled being
   deprecated since we cannot remove it until after we require macOS
   15.0.
 - mac_min_sdk defaults to 12 (overriding Chrome's 15)
 - Mac bot candidates: remove Mac-11, add Mac-15

commit.subject: Rolling build dependencies
commit.message:
Rolling build dependencies

Rolls a bunch of build dependencies, which also required:

 - Rolling ANGLE and VMA for a suppression of -Wthread-safety-analysis
 - Rolling googletest for a narrowing warning fix.
 - Updating the Abseil BUILD.gn files.
 - Adding the download of objdump as the toolchain now uses llvm-otool.
 - Disabling the use of libatomic that we don't have as a dep.
 - Disable -Wnrvo that warns when RVO cannot be applied and has a ton of
   false positives (cases we don't care to fix).
 - Suppress an MSVC warning for Abseil's symbolize_win32.cc that includes
   conflicting Windows headers.
 - Silence warnings about MTLCompileOptions.fastMathEnabled being
   deprecated since we cannot remove it until after we require macOS
   15.0.
 - mac_min_sdk defaults to 12 (overriding Chrome's 15)
 - Mac bot candidates: remove Mac-11, add Mac-15
 - CMake: suppress -Wredundant-parens in third_party/abseil

commit.subject: Rolling build dependencies
commit.message:
Rolling build dependencies

Rolls a bunch of build dependencies, which also required:

 - Rolling ANGLE and VMA for a suppression of -Wthread-safety-analysis
 - Rolling googletest for a narrowing warning fix.
 - Updating the Abseil BUILD.gn files.
 - Adding the download of objdump as the toolchain now uses llvm-otool.
 - Disabling the use of libatomic that we don't have as a dep.
 - Disable -Wnrvo that warns when RVO cannot be applied and has a ton of
   false positives (cases we don't care to fix).
 - Suppress an MSVC warning for Abseil's symbolize_win32.cc that includes
   conflicting Windows headers.
 - Silence warnings about MTLCompileOptions.fastMathEnabled being
   deprecated since we cannot remove it until after we require macOS
   15.0.
 - mac_min_sdk defaults to 12 (overriding Chrome's 15)
 - Mac bot candidates: remove Mac-11, add Mac-15
 - CMake: suppress -Wredundant-parens in third_party/abseil
 - Suppress Clang's -Wredundant-parens from protobuf header included from IR
   protobuf code

commit.message:
Rolling build dependencies

Rolls a bunch of build dependencies, which also required:

 - Rolling ANGLE and VMA for a suppression of -Wthread-safety-analysis

commit.subject: Deduce more type parameters in LRUCache implicitly
commit.message:
Deduce more type parameters in LRUCache implicitly

Allow using default abseil compatible hash and equality functors instead
of specifying CacheFuncs for types which already have them.

Deduce the Error type from the ReturnType of the CacheFn instead of
specifying it as an explicit type parameter.

Also, change the CacheFn parameter type to const Key& instead of Key&.

Change-Id: I6a6a6964958a069e294392f93779dd0c41872b5b

commit.message:
Deduce more type parameters in LRUCache implicitly

Allow using default abseil compatible hash and equality functors instead
of specifying CacheFuncs for types which already have them.

Deduce the Error type from the ReturnType of the CacheFn instead of
specifying it as an explicit type parameter.

Also, change the CacheFn parameter type to const Key& instead of Key&.

commit.subject: [hlsl] Remove list of entry points from writer output
commit.message:
[hlsl] Remove list of entry points from writer output

The backend assumes that it is only generating a single entry point,
so we do not need to return a list. This simplifies the code at the
callsites in Tint that validate the generated HLSL.

This also removes the last build dependency on the `wgsl` directory
from `hlsl`, by switching over to the IR version of the PipelineStage
enum.

Change-Id: I0e63e76e9ce5d7fabe42745a493006b67b1e74fb

commit.subject: [emscripten] Fix GetFeatures/GetWGSLLanguageFeatures with Closure
commit.message:
[emscripten] Fix GetFeatures/GetWGSLLanguageFeatures with Closure

The object keys in this generated reverse-lookup table were getting
minified by Closure. Fix this by making it work like other string-to-int
conversions. This has the added bonus of getting rid of those tables,
reducing the generated code size.

New tests reprduce the issue and verify the fix.

to infra/config/global/ will not actually take effect until

Handle DAWN_DISABLE_LOGGING in android builds

When attempting to build fuzzers on android the build fails with
AndroidLogPriority not beeing used, this is an attempt to fix that by
conditioning on DAWN_DISABLE_LOGGING.

The actual usage of AndroidLogPriority is done later on the same file,
within a branch where not DAWN_DISABLE_LOGGING.

commit.subject: [dawn][emscripten] Fixes some signed to unsigned issues in JS functions.
commit.message:
[dawn][emscripten] Fixes some signed to unsigned issues in JS functions.

- Introduces two helpers to both document and make it clear when unsigned
  WASM integers should be interpreted as unsigned. For a lot of the cases,
  the values are expected to be smaller than 2^31 and hence we can add an
  assert that they are <= 0 before passing the value into JS functions.
  In some cases, the values passed from WASM may be larger than 2^31 and
  in those cases, we need to apply the >>>= 0 workaround before passing
  the values into JS functions.

Change-Id: I2e3bddbb848f3e4950724173e62b8c7f14e93c95

commit.subject: Use TextureView IDs to query VkFramebuffer cache
commit.message:
Use TextureView IDs to query VkFramebuffer cache

Previously the framebuffer cache was using WeakPtrs to TextureViews to
generate the hash, but this turned out to be fairly expensive as we
needed to promote the WeakPtr to a Ref for each attachment every time
we did a cache lookup. Unfortunately this made the framebuffer cache
almost as expensive as simply re-creating the framebuffers.

By switching to use a Device-unique ID for texture views during the
cache lookup we avoid all of that overhead.

Bug: 416088623
Change-Id: I8db50bbbb9f97d10bcbd148a5561fbd7b02b60ca

commit.subject: [metal] Set up a Tint ICE callback for the IR module
commit.message:
[metal] Set up a Tint ICE callback for the IR module

This will capture ICEs generated by the Tint MSL backend and turn them
into Dawn errors, before returning control back to Tint to crash.

This should result in the error messages appearing in our crash dumps
when they occur as part of creating a pipeline from Graphite.

Bug: 434966794, 429983854
Change-Id: I69f84d155f3ca005c0eb74c9718ddef0597e2d50

commit.subject: [tint][fuzz] Add testing for gatherWgslFiles
commit.message:
[tint][fuzz] Add testing for gatherWgslFiles

Adding this test took me slightly down the rabbit hole, since I wanted
to simply check if a dir is empty without needing to walk the
directory structure, which should be doable using os.ReadDir. This led
me to discovering that our OS wrapper did not implement ReadDir(),
which inturn led me to discovering afero's implementation of ReadDir
is not API compatible with os's, it actually implements the older
`Readdir()` (yes with a lowercase d) from File.

So I have added `Readdir` to the wrapper API to match closer the
behaviour that is currently going on/what afero acutally
implements. And added related testing and updated existing tests I was
walking the directory struct manually.

Change-Id: I3ca3087db36445ec9c27c95ba361f94a94d4f384

commit.subject: Move generated LUCI files
commit.message:
Move generated LUCI files

Moves the generated LUCI config files from
//infra/config/global/generated to //infra/config/global/generated/luci.
This should be a functional no-op.

This is in line with what Chromium does and is a prerequisite for some
upcoming Starlark changes for several reasons:

1. We'll be generating significantly more files in the near future, so
   it is helpful to group them appropriately.
2. The Starlark code we are taking a dependency on currently assumes
   that the generated LUCI files are in a luci/ subdirectory. While this
   should be fixed in the longer term, moving these files will unblock
   us sooner.

Bug: 385317083
Change-Id: Ib60f354d94833dc13abc8e653d213d76073eec7d

commit.subject: [emscripten] Fix memory management of WGPUCompilationInfo
commit.message:
[emscripten] Fix memory management of WGPUCompilationInfo

library_webgpu.js would allocate space for WGPUCompilationMessages and
their strings and Utf16 chain structs, even if there were no messages.
Fix library_webgpu.js and webgpu.cpp so they're in sync about when they
need to malloc/free.

- Fixes a UB crash when trying to access messages[0] to free the Utf16
  chain but there isn't actually a messages[0] at all. (This is only
  caught by the test in ASAN builds.)
- Fixes a leak of the string allocation when there is no messages[0] so
  the freeing code can't get the pointer to free. (This is definitely a
  leak because we always allocate at least one byte. The other two
  allocations may also have leaked, but their allocation sizes were 0.)

Tangentially, add -sSAFE_HEAP to debug builds (though this does not
catch the bug, that requires a real ASAN build).

Fixed: 429140232
Change-Id: Iab2f11e4cbceaa568a7c6633e2501dc3bbb1ce87

instructions, so that it actually unshadows them.

address crbug.com/435448004. This is relatively low risk, since it's

[tint] Add ICE callback mechanism

This enables all of the TINT_* macros that produce ICEs to accept an
optional parameter that provides a callback. Without this argument
they behave the same as they do today.

Add unit tests for the variants that use callbacks, and improve the
existing tests to ensure that the errors contain the source line
information.

commit.message:
[tint] Add ICE callback mechanism

This enables all of the TINT_* macros that produce ICEs to accept an
optional parameter that provides a callback. Without this argument
they behave the same as they do today.

Add unit tests for the variants that use callbacks, and improve the
existing tests to ensure that the errors contain the source line
information.

commit.message:
[infra] Add dependency injection support to more fileutils API

Adds the ability to pass in a oswrapper.* to IsDir(), IsExe(),
IsFile(), CopyFile(), and CopyDir() to allow better testing of code
that uses these functions.

Testing is added for these functions.

CopyFile & CopyDir were significantly rewritten due to issues found
when testing.

Updates all of the callsites to use the new API. Some places where I
was making these changes I also changed calls to os.* to be to
oswrapper.*.

[tint][fuzz] Implement corpus generation in Go

This implementation is planned to replace the existing standalone
Python script. That script is retained for now, since the build
recipes depend on it. Once this CL has landed and rolled, the build
recipes will be updated, and a follow on CL can remove the no longer
needed Python version.

Also includes a few incidental cleanups, including moving all of the
TODOs related to testing to the top of the file, since there is
multiple different issues that need to be resolved to be able to
implement testing coverage in this file, and I was tired of trying to
keep the TODOs attached to specific functions.

commit.subject: [tint][fuzz] Support generating IR corpus on the fly
commit.message:
[tint][fuzz] Support generating IR corpus on the fly

Changes the behaviour of `fuzz -ir` to generate the IR corpus on the
fly if the default, WGSL, corpus is being used. Also requires -out
being set when -generate is used, because otherwise it just writes to
a tmp dir that is deleted on exit.

Bug: 348698576, 431997412
Change-Id: Iad92d43e85bfa0f606f9ba840569f4e286f1a973

commit.message:
[tint] For loop analysis for specific use case against fxc

Under specific conditions FXC expects a for/while loop to have a
condition to verify uniformity (detecting varying control flow).

This used to work in AST because we preserved for loops from wgsl to
hlsl.

In our switch to IR we need to detect and then  reconstruct the
condition.

end2end test proven fail now success:
https://dawn-review.googlesource.com/c/dawn/+/253875

commit.subject: [tint][fuzz] Various code improvements for fuzz cmd
commit.message:
[tint][fuzz] Various code improvements for fuzz cmd

- Changed the internal tracking for fuzz mode from bool to enum
- Added more logging to indicate progress of task
- Added more verbose logging for cmds being run
- Unified on using printing for logging, instead of a mix of log.* and
  basic print commands, since the standard logger just prints to the
  console anyway
- Refactored the check for dictionary.txt up to run() from the
  generate args function, which allows removing an error handling path
- Switched the dependency checker code to use a switch block instead of
  an if chain

Change-Id: I2eac8bbbdd83802c4cc22536bf519916db56ddcb

commit.message:
[github] Use CMake to fetch deps in Emdawnwebgpu release jobs

Replace (most of) the custom dependency fetching in
package-emdawnwebgpu.sh in favor of DAWN_FETCH_DEPENDENCIES (which also
does a shallow fetch). Fetching the other dependencies surprisingly only
took an extra 22 seconds when tested on GitHub Actions, and it will be
needed if we start publishing prebuilt native binaries anyway.

This should fix the release jobs on GitHub Actions which currently fail
due to a missing Tint dependency on protobuf. (We don't actually need to
build Tint on that job, but we don't have a CMake option to disable
building Tint, and we don't need one if we just fetch all the deps.)

skip emitting the vertex pulling and any other internal Dawn buffer when

commit.subject: [msl] Allow a group to be specified into bindings.
commit.message:
[msl] Allow a group to be specified into bindings.

When separating into argument buffers we want to keep the binding group
so we can split each bind group into an argument buffer. By default, we
set the value to `0`. When using argument buffers we set the value to
the originating group.

commit.message:
Fix textureutils.cpp to comply with WebGPU Spec

In the WebGPU
spec(https://gpuweb.github.io/gpuweb/#texture-formats-tier1), when Tier
1 is enabled, only R8Snorm/RG8Snorm/RGBA8Snorm support the resolve
functionality. This change modifies the functions in TextureUtils.cpp to
meet these requirements.

commit.message:
Range Analysis: Compute range of Binary with `Modulo` operator

This patch computes the range of a `Binary` with `Modulo` operator.
Given the binary expression with `Modulo` operator `a % b`:
- `a` must be non-negative
- `b` must be a constant positive integer

commit.subject: [tint][infra] Add -generate flag to ./tools/run fuzz
commit.message:
[tint][infra] Add -generate flag to ./tools/run fuzz

This flag adds in the ability to generate fuzzers copora using the
fuzz CLI. This is currently achieved by forking out to the existing
generate_tint_corpus.py, but in the future will have an internal Go
implementation of this logic.

This CL also contains significant refactoring of the existing code in
support of this new feature or for future testing, including:
- Splitting up the 'tool' struct into seperate cmd and task configs
- Moving all the members that previous existed into free functions
- Actually using the custom display usage

Bug: 348698576, 431997412

Change-Id: I5e5998e6cd5a23b0898ef124adca0966c3dc684c

commit.subject: [cmake] Make DAWN_BUILD_MONOLITHIC_LIB control STATIC vs. SHARED.
commit.message:
[cmake] Make DAWN_BUILD_MONOLITHIC_LIB control STATIC vs. SHARED.

Due to how the bundling process works, the monolithic library will only
be monolithic if BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF, otherwise we don't bundle
objects from other SHARED libraries. Make the flag a tri-state:
OFF/STATIC/SHARED and make it control the type of bundled library that
is produced.

Bug:
Change-Id: I9b507d5965c6c088b1c2b3d438690fca6194e2e7

commit.message:
[wgsl] Add chromium_print language feature

The idea is that this will always be advertised as an available
language feature, but might turn into a no-op (with a warning) if the
device cannot support printing for a given pipeline.

This makes it easy for developers to use print, without having to
enable an extension on the adapter and at the top of a shader.

commit.subject: Refactor WaitForQueueSerial to eliminate race condition
commit.message:
Refactor WaitForQueueSerial to eliminate race condition

The `WaitForQueueSerial()` function was susceptible to a race
condition because its implementation was divided into several
non-atomic steps that could execute in parallel across multiple
threads:
- `queue->WaitForQueueSerial()`
- `queue->CheckAndUpdateCompletedSerials()`
- Update `mCompletedSerial`
- Trigger callbacks
- Poll future completion statuses

This parallelism could lead to correctness issues. For example, a
thread could successfully complete its wait, but before it could
update `mCompletedSerial`, another thread might process all the
passed fences. This would result in the first thread losing
information about the actual completed serial.

This commit resolves the race condition by updating the completed
serial immediately after a successful wait, ensuring the state is
updated atomically and preventing lost serial information.

Bug: 430401631
Change-Id: I5997f41bf26d44ad08132333fecfd42760e9e1a7

commit.subject: [dawn][opengl] Add for binding_array<texture> builtin emulation.
commit.message:
[dawn][opengl] Add for binding_array<texture> builtin emulation.

The emulation of builtins like textureNumLevels in the GL backend use a
UBO to contain the metadata of the texture. Support for binding_array
needs to be added by registering in Dawn that all elements of the array
need their data added to the UBO.

And add a test.

Bug: 427409135
Change-Id: I294795573c2baa061d574c406da5b5019582aa2a

commit.subject: Add e2e tests for Tier1 read-only storage texture access
commit.message:
Add e2e tests for Tier1 read-only storage texture access

Add end-to-end tests for STORAGE_BINDING (read-only) for a range of TextureFormatsTier1 formats, including: r16unorm, r16snorm, rg16unorm, r16snorm, rgba16unorm, rgba16snorm, r8unorm, r8snorm, r8uint, r8sint, rg8unorm, rg8snorm, rg8uint, rg8sint, r16uint, r16sint, r16float, rg16uint, rg16sint, rg16float, rgb10a2uint, rgb10a2unorm， rg11b10ufloat. These tests confirm proper GPUStorageTextureAccess when TextureFormatsTier1 is enabled.

Bug: 421941589
Change-Id: I29624668d7253bbaf17bcdc0bf7ca98c295d5bbf

commit.subject: Enable TextureFormatsTier1 in Vulkan backend
commit.message:
Enable TextureFormatsTier1 in Vulkan backend

This commit enables the `texture-formats-tier1` WebGPU extension in the Vulkan backend.
Enablement conditions:
1.  Vulkan device supports `shaderStorageImageExtendedFormats`.
2.  Specific formats (`r16unorm`, `r16snorm`, `rg16unorm`, `rg16snorm`, `rgba16unorm`, `rgba16snorm`, `r8snorm`, `rg8snorm`, `rgba8snorm`, `rg11b10float`) must support both `VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT` and `VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BLEND_BIT` in optimal tiling.

Bug: 421941589
Change-Id: Idd3449a14f82aa51afefeda1b5b38081f688903d

commit.subject: Test `ShaderRobustnessPerf` with Integer Range Analysis disabled
commit.message:
Test `ShaderRobustnessPerf` with Integer Range Analysis disabled

This patch adds the configuration that disables Integer Range
Analysis in `ShaderRobustnessPerf` in dawn_perf_tests. As Integer
Range Analysis is enabled by default in DawnPlatform.cpp, it is
more convenient to compare the performance difference with and
without Integer Range Analysis by adding a configuration to explicitly
disable it.

Bug: 348701956
Change-Id: Id1cead7980dc5bbe0d3016abaa4e6ca5411bd94d

commit.subject: [tint][fuzz] Add --ir to ./tools/run fuzz
commit.message:
[tint][fuzz] Add --ir to ./tools/run fuzz

This adds basic support for running and checking the tint_ir_fuzzer to
the tool. Passing in this flag will have the tool run in IR mode,
which will use the tint_ir_fuzzer instead of the tint_wgsl_fuzzer.

If no corpus directory is supplied, then none will be used instead of
trying to use the default WGSL corpus directory. This means that just
running the fuzzer without supplying a corpus will have it run without
any seeding, and attempting to use `--check` without supplying a
corpus will fail (with an appropriate error message).

Future CLs will migrate generating to IR corpus to this tool, and thus
allow it to have more sensible defaults.

Bug: 348698576
Change-Id: I0a28df3ff276c2948614d1633db4765c07276a01

commit.subject: [dawn][opengl] Correctly allocate builtin metadata between stages.
commit.message:
[dawn][opengl] Correctly allocate builtin metadata between stages.

Some texture builtins that query metadata need to be emulated by passing
that data in a UBO. Multiple stages may used such metadata which caused
issues with the previous approach to allocating an offset in the UBO for
the metadata. Replace it with a "registrar" that reuses the same offset
if possible.

Also message the datastructure storing the Dawn-side information of what
metadata needs to be put where to make it subjectively a bit nicer, and
use a FlatBindingIndex instead of BindGroupIndex+BindingIndex to address
it.

Bug: 427409135
Change-Id: I1326434517cadc782c683bfdd60aeae1fe9c1992

commit.subject: [dawn][native] Simplifies DeviceGuard with DeviceMutex.
commit.message:
[dawn][native] Simplifies DeviceGuard with DeviceMutex.

- Moves the defer object to be a part of the DeviceMutex instead of
  the Device. This allows for simplifying cases where the device
  might be destroyed since the Defer now lives with the DeviceMutex
  on the additional Ref that it holds.
- This change also moves the code in Mutex around a bit so that the
  calls to Lock and Unlock are the ones responsible for updating
  state used for ASSERT checks. This is necessary to later expose
  private Lock/Unlock helpers in the Device class to implement
  unlocking before calling WaitFor* functions.

Bug: 412761228
